boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Nashville record (December 15-16, 1864) in the Franklin-Nashville Campaign [September-December 1864]. Murfreesboro (TN037, December 5-7) precedes it; the pursuit to the Tennessee River after December 16 is outside the record. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force text names the IV and XXIII Corps, the detachment of the Army of the Tennessee, a provisional detachment and the cavalry corps against the Army of Tennessee, with no numbers; the live field reads zeros. Cox says Smith's three divisions aggregated nearly 12,000, Steedman brought 5,200 of 8,000 from Chattanooga, about 8,000 were detached at Murfreesboro, Thomas had about 6,000 infantry and artillery and 3,000 cavalry at Nashville on November 30, the cavalry present for duty numbered 10,884 of which 2,272 were dismounted, and Cruft's division exceeded 5,000 by December 14. On Hood's own loss figures Cox puts Hood's army at about 44,000. Hood's addenda give an effective total of 23,053 on December 10; Hood reports about 6,000 Union troops at Murfreesborough.
claims.rationale: Mixed dates, bases and scopes (aggregates, present for duty, effective; detached garrisons); Cox's 44,000 is his own reconstruction. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Hood says his right repulsed the attacks but, after Bate's division gave way at 3.30 p.m. on the 16th, his whole line broke and retreated in great confusion; Cox says the Confederate left was 'crushed in like an egg-shell'; NPS says Hood's army fled.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 6,602 (US 2,140; CS 4,462); the live field reads 9,561 (US 3,061; CS 6,500). Cox gives Thomas's losses as 3,057, fewer than 400 killed, and the capture of about 4,500 prisoners and 53 guns (1,200 prisoners and 16 guns on the first day). Hood gives his artillery loss as 54 guns and says his killed and wounded were small and his prisoners not great; he says his losses for the whole campaign, including prisoners, did not exceed 10,000.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Hood's campaign total is context, not a Nashville count.

open_questions: Thomas's No. 1 report and the Nos. 2–7 abstracts, organization and casualty returns, Wood's, Smith's, Schofield's, Steedman's and Wilson's reports, Lee's, Stewart's, Bate's and the other Confederate reports, Hood's January 20, 1865 inspection abstract (garbled), and Cox's Appendix A tables (garbled in OCR) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Jacob D. Cox's The March to the Sea; Franklin and Nashville (1882) is an interested history by the commander of the Twenty-third Corps' Third Division (and, at Franklin, of both divisions of that corps) that draws on official papers. Corse's, French's, R. S. Granger's, Doolittle's, Sinclair's, Forrest's, Hood's and Rousseau's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXIX part 1 and XLV part 1, are separate families of interested accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
